source_note: New source-grounded practice MCQs generated from the two text-based PDFs. The image-only 'PHY 104 Questions.pdf' is not included; it needs OCR or manual transcription before its past questions can be added.

questions.text: In simple harmonic motion, the restoring force is
options: proportional to the square of displacement
proportional to displacement and directed toward the mean position
questions.explanation: SHM is defined by F = -kx: the force is linear in displacement and always restores toward equilibrium.

questions.text: The acceleration of a particle executing SHM is given by
questions.explanation: Differentiating y = a sin(ωt) twice gives a = -ω²y.

questions.text: At the mean position of an SHM oscillator,
options: kinetic energy is maximum and potential energy is zero
potential energy is maximum and kinetic energy is zero
questions.explanation: At y = 0 the speed is greatest, so K = ½mω²a² and U = 0.

questions.text: At an extreme position of an SHM oscillator,
options: kinetic energy is maximum and potential energy is zero
potential energy is maximum and kinetic energy is zero
questions.explanation: At y = ±a the speed is zero, so U = ½mω²a² and K = 0.

questions.text: The total mechanical energy of an SHM oscillator is proportional to
options: the square of the instantaneous velocity
questions.explanation: E = ½mω²a², so total energy scales with a².

questions.text: The period of a simple pendulum depends on
options: its length and the gravitational acceleration
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g); mass does not appear in the ideal simple-pendulum formula.

questions.text: For a spring-mass oscillator, increasing the attached mass
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k), so a larger m gives a longer period.

questions.text: For a spring-mass oscillator, increasing the spring constant
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(m/k), so a stiffer spring gives a shorter period.

questions.text: The phase of a vibrating particle determines its
options: position and direction of motion relative to the mean position
questions.explanation: Phase is the argument of the sine or cosine function and fixes the state of motion.

questions.text: Angular frequency ω is related to ordinary frequency f by
questions.explanation: One cycle corresponds to 2π radians, so ω = 2πf.

questions.text: The SI unit of angular frequency is
questions.explanation: Angular frequency is measured in radians per second.

questions.text: A non-harmonic oscillation is
options: a single sine or cosine function
a motion with no restoring force
a wave that needs no medium
a combination of two or more harmonic oscillations
questions.explanation: The lecture notes define non-harmonic oscillation as a sum of two or more harmonic terms.

questions.text: Damped oscillations are characterised by
options: constant energy in spite of friction
questions.explanation: Damping forces such as friction remove energy, so amplitude decays exponentially.

questions.text: Resonance occurs when
options: the driving frequency is twice the natural frequency
the driving frequency equals the natural frequency
questions.explanation: At resonance the external force matches the natural frequency and the response is largest.

questions.text: An ideal free oscillation has
questions.explanation: Free oscillations proceed at the natural frequency with no energy loss in the ideal case.

questions.text: Forced oscillations are sustained by
questions.explanation: A forced oscillator is driven by an external periodic force.

questions.text: Coupled oscillations involve
options: two or more linked particles whose motions influence one another
a single isolated mass on a spring
questions.explanation: Coupled SHM links two or more particles, e.g. masses joined by a spring.

questions.text: Maintained oscillations compensate energy losses by
options: supplying energy from an external source
questions.explanation: A maintained oscillator receives energy from outside to replace dissipated energy.

questions.text: Normal modes are best described as
options: collective patterns of motion in a coupled system
questions.explanation: Normal modes are the characteristic coordinated motions of coupled oscillators.

questions.text: The Q value of a resonant system is associated with
options: the speed of sound in a vacuum
the beat frequency of two notes
the sharpness of its power response curve
questions.explanation: The course outline links Q values with resonance and power response curves.

questions.text: A wave transfers
options: energy without permanently displacing the medium
questions.explanation: A wave is a disturbance that carries energy while the medium oscillates about equilibrium.

questions.text: Mechanical waves
options: require a material medium for propagation
questions.explanation: Water waves, sound and waves on a string need a material medium.

questions.text: Electromagnetic waves
options: do not require a material medium
questions.explanation: Light, radio waves, X-rays and gamma rays propagate without a material medium.

questions.text: In a transverse wave, the vibration of the medium is
options: perpendicular to the direction of travel
parallel to the direction of travel
questions.explanation: Transverse waves have particle motion at right angles to propagation.

questions.text: In a longitudinal wave, the vibration of the medium is
options: parallel to the direction of travel
perpendicular to the direction of travel
questions.explanation: Longitudinal waves have particle motion along the direction of propagation.

questions.text: For a sinusoidal wave y = A sin(kx - ωt), the wave speed is
questions.explanation: The phase velocity of y = A sin(kx - ωt) is v = ω/k.

questions.text: The angular wave number k is related to wavelength λ by
questions.explanation: One wavelength corresponds to a phase change of 2π radians.

questions.text: For any periodic wave, wave speed v, frequency f and wavelength λ satisfy
questions.explanation: One wavelength passes per period, so speed equals frequency times wavelength.

questions.text: Phase velocity and group velocity
options: apply only to sound in pipes
are both zero in a vacuum
are generally different in a dispersive medium
questions.explanation: Dispersion makes the phase and group velocities differ; the course outline lists both.

questions.text: The wave equation in two and three dimensions generalises
options: the one-dimensional wave equation to higher-dimensional propagation
questions.explanation: The outline explicitly includes 2-D and 3-D wave equations.

questions.text: Waves at interfaces are mainly studied in terms of
questions.explanation: The course outline lists waves at interfaces together with energy and power of waves.

questions.text: The principle of superposition states that the resultant displacement is
options: the product of the individual displacements
the algebraic sum of the individual wave displacements
questions.explanation: For linear waves, yR = y1 + y2 + ...

questions.text: Waves that obey the principle of superposition are called
questions.explanation: The lecture note calls waves that obey superposition linear waves.

questions.text: Constructive interference occurs when superposed displacements are
questions.explanation: Same-direction displacements add to give a larger resultant.

questions.text: Destructive interference occurs when superposed displacements are
questions.explanation: Opposite displacements partially or completely cancel.

questions.text: Diffraction is the
options: bending of waves around obstacles or apertures
change of frequency at a boundary
questions.explanation: The lecture note defines diffraction as bending around corners of an obstacle or aperture.

questions.text: Diffraction becomes more pronounced when
options: the aperture is small compared with the wavelength
the aperture is very large compared with the wavelength
questions.explanation: A smaller aperture relative to λ gives stronger spreading.

questions.text: Polarization is possible only for
questions.explanation: Polarization confines vibration to one plane, which requires transverse vibration.

questions.text: Polarization of light is evidence that light is
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarized, so polarized light proves transverse character.

questions.text: Sound waves in air are
questions.explanation: Sound requires a medium and its particle vibration is along the propagation direction.

questions.text: Sound cannot propagate through
questions.explanation: Sound is mechanical and needs a material medium.

questions.text: The speed of sound is generally greatest in
questions.explanation: The notes give roughly 6000 m/s in solids, 1480 m/s in liquids and 330-343 m/s in air.

questions.text: Sound intensity is defined as
options: power per unit area perpendicular to the wave
questions.explanation: I = Power/Area, with units W/m².

questions.text: The decibel scale is
questions.explanation: β = 10 log10(I/I0) is a logarithmic measure.

questions.text: The standard threshold of hearing intensity I0 is
questions.explanation: The notes use I0 = 10⁻¹² W/m² as the reference intensity.

questions.text: The pitch of a musical note mainly depends on its
questions.explanation: Higher frequency gives higher pitch.

questions.text: The loudness of a sound mainly depends on its
questions.explanation: Loudness is the sensation associated with intensity, which scales with amplitude squared.

questions.text: The quality or timbre of a note depends on
questions.explanation: Quality lets the ear distinguish notes of the same pitch and loudness.

questions.text: The approximate audible frequency range for humans quoted in the notes is
questions.explanation: The lecture note gives 15 - 20,000 Hz for human audio frequency.

questions.text: The Doppler effect is a change in observed frequency caused by
options: relative motion between source and observer
questions.explanation: Relative motion changes the apparent frequency of a wave.

questions.text: An echo is produced by
questions.explanation: Echoes are reflected sound waves returning to the listener.

questions.text: Beats are heard when
options: a single pure tone is played
two notes of slightly different frequencies sound together
questions.explanation: Beats are periodic loudness variations from superposing close frequencies.

questions.text: The beat frequency of two notes f1 and f2 is
questions.explanation: The notes give fbeat = f1 - f2, i.e. the magnitude of the difference.

questions.text: Reverberation is the persistence of sound
questions.explanation: The notes define reverberation as persistence of sound after the source ceases.

questions.text: A closed pipe supports
questions.explanation: The notes derive f0, 3f0, 5f0, ... for a closed pipe.

questions.text: An open pipe supports
questions.explanation: The notes derive f0, 2f0, 3f0, ... for an open pipe.

questions.text: In a resonance tube, the end correction arises because
options: the node is below the closed end
the antinode is slightly above the open end
questions.explanation: The notes state that the antinode at the top does not exactly coincide with the tube opening.

questions.text: At the closed end of a vibrating air column there is always
questions.explanation: Air particles cannot move at a closed end, giving a node.

questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is approximately
questions.explanation: The lecture note gives C ≈ 3.0 × 10⁸ m/s.

questions.text: For light, speed c, frequency f and wavelength λ satisfy
questions.explanation: The lecture note states C = fλ.

questions.text: The law of reflection states that
options: light always bends toward the normal
the angle of incidence is twice the angle of reflection
the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
questions.explanation: Specular reflection has equal incident and reflected angles measured from the normal.

questions.text: Refraction occurs because light
options: changes speed when it enters a different medium
questions.explanation: The notes describe refraction as a change in speed from one medium to another.

questions.text: Snell's law states that for a given pair of media
options: sin i / sin r is constant
sin i × sin r is constant
questions.explanation: The second law of refraction is η = sin i / sin r.

questions.text: Total internal reflection requires light to travel
options: from a higher to a lower refractive index above the critical angle
from a lower to a higher refractive index
questions.explanation: Beyond the critical angle, refraction ceases and reflection becomes total.

questions.text: A convex lens is
questions.explanation: The notes describe convex lenses as converging lenses.

questions.text: A concave lens is
options: a source of total internal reflection
questions.explanation: The notes describe concave lenses as diverging lenses.

questions.text: The power of a lens is defined as
options: the reciprocal of its focal length
the ratio of image height to object height
questions.explanation: The notes give P = 1/f, with lens power in dioptres.

questions.text: Dispersion of light is the separation of colours because
questions.explanation: The notes attribute dispersion and chromatic aberration to wavelength-dependent refractive index.

questions.text: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as
questions.explanation: The course outline lists Huygens' principle with interference and diffraction.

questions.text: Interference and diffraction of light provide evidence for
questions.explanation: These are classic wave phenomena listed under wave optics.

questions.text: A Polaroid produces
questions.explanation: The notes describe plane polarization using a Polaroid or calcite/tourmaline crystal.

questions.text: The velocity of light
options: is the same in every medium
equals the speed of sound in air
depends on the medium through which it travels
questions.explanation: The lecture note states that light velocity depends on the medium.

questions.text: Light waves are
questions.explanation: Light needs no medium and can be polarized, so it is transverse electromagnetic radiation.

questions.text: Scattering of light refers to
options: redirection of light by particles or irregularities
questions.explanation: The course outline lists scattering of light under optics.

questions.text: Optical instruments form images using
questions.explanation: The outline includes thin lenses and optical instruments.
